sentences.en: Today I go to the store to buy things.
One book costs twenty yuan, and I bought one.
I also bought fruit, ten yuan.
Now I don't have much money left.
I won't buy anything more; I am going home.

quiz.q: Where does the narrator go today?
How much does one book cost?
What else does the narrator buy?

grammar.e: 有 means 'to have' or 'there is'. Its negative is 没有, never 不有.
grammar.x: 我有一些钱。 — I have some money.

grammar.p: Measure words 本 and 块
grammar.e: Chinese counts nouns with a measure word: 一本书 (one book), 二十块钱 (twenty yuan). 一 is read yì before a third-tone syllable like běn.
grammar.x: 一本书二十块钱。 — One book costs twenty yuan.

grammar.p: 了 at the end — a new situation
grammar.e: Sentence-final 了 says something has changed: 不多了 = there isn't much left now, though there was before.
grammar.x: 现在我的钱不多了。 — Now I don't have much money left.
